Biochemist here. I just popped open my Bio Psych book from college to answer the question as to why you're having cravings.

Weed is technically physically addictive (read: habit forming) as we've found it has an affect on your body's dopamine systems through GABA. All abused drugs increase the release of dopamine in the nucleus accumbens. Cannabinoids do so indirectly. They inhibit GABA release in the ventral segmental area of the midbrain, a major source of axons that release dopamine in the nucleus accumbens. When they inhibit GABA there they decrease inhibition (increasing activity) of the neurons that release dopamine in the nucleus accumbens.

So in short marijuana is physically habit forming, like most drugs, though it's not as serious about it as some drugs.

Rise of the Tomb Raider Contains Sections Which Allow Pacifist Completion Options

Now, we are told that there are sections where combat is unavoidable, which is one of the things turning me off the series...

Really, and why is that? In the first tomb raider you basically just ran around shooting animals, while solving puzzles in between.

These people complaining about the combat in Tomb Raider just really aren't getting it. Yes, more puzzles which takes some grey matter to solve will always be welcome, but let's not pretend that Tomb Raider has never been about combat and lethal violence.

Partly because it's more combat heavy than it used to be. Waves of enemies during action set pieces and the like. But mostly it's the style of it. It doesn't feel like Tomb Raider anymore. At least, not the Tomb Raider I played when I was younger. It's much more slick and cover shooter based. Which works well, and is fine in its own right, it's just not the way I want it to be
